meditation.text: Hello, and welcome, {name}.
Let's set this time aside, just for you.
Find a posture that feels steady and easy, and let the eyes close, or soften toward the floor.
There is nothing to achieve here, and nothing to fix. You can let all of that go for now.
Take one deeper breath, in through the nose, and let it out slowly.
And let the breathing return to its own natural rhythm.
Begin to notice where you feel the breath most clearly. Perhaps the belly, rising and falling. Perhaps the cool air at the tip of the nose.
You do not need to control it. Just feel it, one breath at a time.
The in-breath, arriving.
And the out-breath, leaving.
Feel the weight of the body, settled and supported, held by the floor or the chair.
Before long, the mind will wander, into a thought, a plan, a memory. This is completely normal.
The moment you notice you have drifted, that is the practice working, not failing.
Gently, and without any judgment, guide your attention back to the breath.
Again, the breath in.
And a slow breath out.
There is nowhere else you need to be. Just here, with this breath, and then the next.
Rest in the simple feeling of breathing, {name}.
Take one last easy breath.
And when you are ready, {name}, let the eyes open, and carry this quiet with you.
Hello, {name}. Let's take this time to come home to the body.
Lie down, or sit, however you are most comfortable, and let the eyes close.
Take one long breath, and let the whole body soften as you breathe out.
We are going to travel slowly through the body, one part at a time, with simple attention.
Start at the very top of the head. Just notice whatever is there. Warmth, tingling, or nothing at all.
There is no need to change anything. Only to notice, and to let go.
Let the attention move down to the face. Soften the forehead, the eyes, the jaw.
Down through the neck and the shoulders. Let them drop away from the ears.
Feel the arms, all the way to the hands. Heavy, and at rest.
Notice the chest, rising and falling on its own.
The belly, soft. The back, supported.
If the mind wanders off, that is fine. Just come back to the part of the body you left.
Let the attention settle down through the hips, the legs, and into the feet.
Now feel the body as one whole thing, breathing, and at ease.
Rest here for a moment, {name}, with nothing to do.
Take one more slow breath.
And when you are ready, {name}, let the eyes open, carrying this ease with you.
Hello, {name}. Let's begin by simply listening.
Sit comfortably, and let the eyes close, or lower toward the floor.
For a moment, do not try to meditate at all. Just let the sounds around you come and go.
Near sounds, and far sounds. You do not have to name them, or hold them. Let them pass through.
Notice how each sound arrives, and then dissolves, all on its own.
Now let the sounds fall into the background, and bring your attention to the breath.
We will count the breaths, softly, just to keep the mind gathered.
Breathe in, and as you breathe out, count one.
In again, and out, two.
Continue on your own, up to ten, and then begin again at one.
If you lose count, no problem at all. Just start again from one.
The counting is only a thread, keeping you here, breath after breath.
Let it be easy. There is no right number to reach.
When the mind drifts, the sounds are still here, and the breath is still here.
Now let the counting go, and just sit, {name}, quiet and awake.
Take one last easy breath.
And when you are ready, {name}, open your eyes.

sleep.text: Rest now, {name}. There is nothing left to do today.
Let yourself lie back, and feel the whole weight of you held by the bed.
We will let go of the day by first letting the body work, and then letting it rest.
Gently curl the toes and tighten the feet. Hold for a moment. And release, completely.
Tense the legs now, just a little. Hold. And let them go soft and heavy.
Draw the shoulders up toward the ears. Hold. And let them drop.
Squeeze the hands into loose fists. Hold. And open them, and let them fall still.
Scrunch the face gently. Hold. And smooth it all away.
Feel how each part is warmer, heavier, and more at rest than before.
There is nothing left to hold. The bed is holding all of it for you.
Let the breath slow down on its own, each one a little longer than the last.
With every breath out, you sink a little deeper.
The body, quiet. The day, over.
Let the mind grow soft and slow now, {name}, like the last light fading.
There is nowhere to be but here. Let sleep come, {name}.
Rest now, {name}.
Let the eyes close, and let the bed take your full weight.
Bring a soft, warm attention to the center of the chest, where the breath rises and falls.
Imagine a gentle warmth there, like sun on your skin, spreading a little with each breath.
It moves out across the chest, into the shoulders, softening everything it touches.
Down the arms, all the way to the tips of the fingers. Warm, and heavy.
The warmth spreads down through the belly, and the hips.
Into the legs, slow and heavy, all the way to the feet.
The whole body, warm, heavy, and still.
Each breath out lets you sink a little further into the bed.
There is nothing to hold onto. You can let the day dissolve.
Heavier, and warmer, and slower.
The thoughts of the day drift off, like clouds thinning at dusk.
Let yourself be carried now, {name}, softly, toward sleep.
You are safe. You can let go.
It is the end of the day, {name}. Time to set it all down.
Settle into the bed, and let the eyes close.
Picture yourself laying the day down, the way you would set a heavy bag by the door.
Whatever happened, done or undone, you can leave it there until morning.
Now bring to mind a quiet, safe place. Real or imagined, it does not matter.
Maybe a cabin in the rain. A shore at dusk. A warm room, with soft light.
Look around this place slowly. Notice the colors, the shapes, the stillness.
Hear its soft, far-off sounds. Feel its warmth on your skin.
You have nothing to do here but rest. No one needs anything from you.
With each breath, you sink a little deeper into this quiet.
The day is behind the door. This peaceful place is all around you.
Let the details blur now, and let the scene grow dim and soft.
Let the mind wander wherever it likes, slow and untroubled.
Rest here, {name}, and let sleep find you.
Goodnight, {name}.

flow.text: Let's get you ready to focus, {name}.
Sit tall, both feet flat on the floor, and feel the chair steady beneath you.
Lengthen the spine, and let the shoulders settle down the back.
Take a slow breath in, and let it out completely.
Feel your base. The contact of your feet, the seat beneath you. Solid, and stable.
From that steady base, let the body be both relaxed and awake.
Soft in the face and the hands. Alert through the spine.
This is the posture of focus. Grounded below, and clear above.
Take another breath, and feel a quiet, ready energy gather.
Nothing to rush. Nothing to force. Just a body, prepared.
Calm, and alert. Relaxed, and sharp.
Let the eyes open softly, keeping this grounded, ready feeling.
Carry it into the work, {name}. Settled, and clear.
When you are ready, begin.
Let's find your focus, {name}.
Sit up, tall and easy, and let the eyes close for just a minute.
We are going to sharpen the attention the way you would sharpen any tool. With a little practice.
Take a slow breath in, and out. And we will begin to count.
Breathe in, and out, one. In, and out, two.
Keep going, up to five, and then start again at one.
Each number is a small act of focus. A rep for the mind.
When you notice the count has slipped, that noticing is the focus returning.
No frustration. Just begin again at one.
Feel how the mind steadies the longer you stay with it.
The attention grows quieter, and more precise.
Now let the counting go, and rest in that sharpened, settled state.
This is the focus you will carry into your work, {name}.
Open your eyes, and begin, clear and ready.
Alright, {name}. Let's get you ready.
Sit tall, both feet on the floor, and let the shoulders settle down the back.
Take a slow breath in, and let it go completely.
Notice the swirl of the day, all the tabs open in your mind.
Picture that clutter as sediment, stirred up in a glass of water.
You do not have to push it away. Just stop stirring, and let it settle.
With each breath out, the water grows a little clearer.
Take one more slow, deliberate breath.
And as the water clears, a single thing comes into focus.
Bring to mind the one thing you are here to do.
Hold it simply, without pressure. A clear, quiet intention.
Let your attention gather around it, like light drawn to a single point.
Calm, and alert. Relaxed, and sharp.
This is the state you work from, {name}. Settled, and clear.
Take one last easy breath.
And when you are ready, {name}, open your eyes, and begin.

relax.text: Welcome, {name}. Let's take a little time to unwind.
Settle into your seat, and let yourself fully arrive.
Let the eyes close, or rest softly wherever they land.
Take a slow breath, and as you breathe out, let the shoulders drop.
Notice anywhere you are holding the day in the body. The jaw. The hands. The brow.
You do not have to fix it. Just let each of those places soften, a little at a time.
Unclench the jaw. Let the tongue rest. Smooth the space between the eyebrows.
Let the hands open. Let the belly be soft.
With every breath out, set a little more of the day down.
There is nothing you need to carry right now.
Feel how the body eases when you stop holding it up.
Softer, and slower, and lighter.
Just rest here, {name}, with nothing to do, and nowhere to be.
Stay as long as you like. And when you are ready, {name}, gently return.
Take a breath, {name}. Let's set the day down.
Find a comfortable place to be, and let the body relax into it.
We will calm the whole system through one simple thing. A longer breath out.
Breathe in gently through the nose, to a count of four.
And breathe out, slow and smooth, to a count of six.
The long out-breath is a signal to the body. It says, you are safe. You can rest.
In, for four.
Out, for six.
You may feel the heartbeat ease, and the shoulders drop.
Let each out-breath be a little longer, and a little softer, than the one before.
There is no effort here. Just letting the air leave, slowly.
The body is downshifting, gear by gear, into rest.
Now let the counting fade, and let the breath find its own slow rhythm.
Rest in this ease, {name}.
When you are ready, {name}, carry this calm with you.
Let's slow down together, {name}.
Find a comfortable place, and let your weight settle into it.
Take a long, slow breath, and let it go without any effort.
For the next little while, there is nothing to reach for. This is a pause.
Notice the simple comfort of being still. The support beneath you. The warmth of your own body.
Feel the air on your skin. The quiet in the room.
You do not have to make anything happen. Just receive what is already pleasant.
The weight of rest. The ease of the out-breath. The softness behind the eyes.
Let yourself enjoy it, the way you would savor a warm drink, slowly.
There is nowhere to be. Nothing is being asked of you.
Let the day set, like the sun going down, unhurried.
Soft, and slow, and here.
Rest in this for a while, {name}, and let it fill you back up.
When you are ready, {name}, return gently, and carry the calm with you.

stress-relief.text: Let's ease this together, {name}.
Wherever you are, just find a way to sit or stand that feels steady.
We will settle the body quickly, with the breath.
Take a breath in through the nose. And at the top, take a second, small sip of air.
Now let it all go. A long, slow breath out through the mouth.
That double breath in, and long breath out, is the fastest way to tell the body it is safe.
Let's do it again. A full breath in, and a small sip more.
And a long, complete breath out. Let the shoulders fall.
One more. In, and a little more in.
And a long release. Feel the edge come off.
Let the breath return to normal now, and just notice the body settling.
The wave of stress is already passing. You helped it move through.
Nothing has to be solved this second. You have this breath, and it is steady.
You are okay, {name}. You are here, and you are okay.
When you are ready, {name}, carry this steadier breath back with you.
Let's take the pressure off for a moment, {name}.
Sit however you can, and let the eyes close, if that feels alright.
Take one slow breath, and let it out.
Instead of pushing the stress away, we are going to turn toward it, gently.
Notice what you are feeling right now. See if you can give it a quiet name.
Maybe it is worry. Maybe pressure, or fear, or just too much at once.
You do not have to judge it, or fix it. Just name it, softly. This is worry. This is pressure.
Naming a feeling gives it room, and takes away some of its grip.
Notice where it sits in the body. The chest, the stomach, the throat.
Breathe toward that place, as if making a little space around it.
You can let it be here, without letting it run the show.
Feelings move through, like weather, when we stop bracing against them.
You are bigger than this moment, {name}. It is here, and it will pass.
Take a full breath, and feel your own steadiness underneath it all.
When you are ready, {name}, open your eyes, a little lighter.
Let's come back to solid ground, {name}.
Plant both feet on the floor, and feel them there, firmly.
When the mind is racing ahead, we steady it by coming back to the senses, right here.
Feel your points of contact. The feet on the floor. The back against the seat. The hands, resting.
Look around, without moving much, and notice three things you can see.
Now notice two things you can hear. One near, and one far.
And one thing you can feel. The air, the fabric of your clothes, the temperature of the room.
None of these things are stressful. They are just here. And so are you.
This is the present moment. It is steadier than the story in your head.
Take a slow breath, and feel yourself here, in your body, in this room.
The worry is about somewhere else, some other time. Right here, you are okay.
Feet on the floor. Breath in the body. Solid ground.
Stay here for a moment, {name}, steady and present.
When you are ready, {name}, carry this ground with you.
